narr: Nothing yet on the accusation — Tehran's last words before midnight were the ones it chose on Friday evening: the foreign ministers of Iran, Iraq and the Gulf states convene in Oman on Monday on the Iran–Oman 'safe routes', 'a significant development' toward 'shared regional security … avoiding the destructive and divisive interference of extra-regional actors'; Iran 'is committed to ensure the security of navigation' — but 'as long as aggressive actions and illegal interventions by the United States, including maritime blockades and economic warfare, persist, the security of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz cannot be guaranteed.' Around it the Axis still claims the Red Sea (Aref: 'the victories of the heroic people of Yemen'; the Friday-prayers leader: the strait is in the IRGC's 'powerful grip'). Now Riyadh says drones from Iraq — Iran's other ally — hit the pipeline on Thursday morning, and names no militia and no Iran; Baghdad, which sits at Monday's table, has ordered an investigation. Mehr's English wire has nothing after 18:00 Tehran. Whether Tehran denies, deflects to the 'Iraqi resistance' or says nothing before Monday is the tell.
Mehr 247656 · Al Jazeera (Tehran) · SPA via Arab News · Sep 11

On the pipeline, nothing: CNN's two US officials confirmed pump stations were struck by drones 'originating from Iraq' with 'extensive fire damage' at one, and the State Department, the White House and CENTCOM declined to comment; CENTCOM's newest release is still Sep 8. The day's line came from the 9/11 stage — Hegseth: 'We control the strait. We will finish this fight'; Trump: 'That's why we fight today … There can only be victory' — and neither touched Monday's Oman table. Thursday's refusal of a second front against the Houthis stands, and now Riyadh has been hit from the north as well and asked nobody to strike back. At the UN the US will 'look to partners in the coming days to weigh options'; Bessent names a large bank Monday. August CPI hot on gasoline, diesel a record $6.06, a ~90% priced Fed hike Wednesday. 'We control the strait' — seven transits Thursday, none crude; and the Hormuz bypass is now shut too.
CNN · Times of Israel · The National · CBS · Sep 11

The whisper at the top of the list became a fact at 19:11 UTC: Saudi Arabia's energy ministry says the East-West pipeline was attacked on Thursday morning and stopped; the foreign ministry says the drones came from Iraq; several people were hurt; two US officials tell CNN a pump station has extensive fire damage. That is a Gulf energy hit by an Iranian proxy — rung 7 by the rules, and the 'Iran strikes GCC territory' signal — and both are HELD for Sam's tick under the approval gate; if ticked, the 60-day 'forced escalation' odds go 50 → 55 and 'deal' 18 → 14, and 'Bigger war' 33 → 35. What moved on its own: the Saudi–UAE pot to 84° (struck component at casualties level). What did not: Riyadh's answer, which is restraint — no retaliation 'at this stage', an 'opportunity' for Baghdad, and no word 'Iran' in the statement, three days before it sits with Araghchi in Oman. Washington declined to comment. Brent closed at $104.4 before the confirmation; Monday opens with the bypass shut and the table set. AIS 24 h: 10 in / 18 out, 29 in the strait. Live 22:01 UTC: one USAF KC-46 over the UAE, nothing over Iran. The dial: 83° / 84° / 84° / 84°.

weak: Saudi Energy Ministry + Foreign Ministry via SPA · Arab News 21:41 · Times of Israel 22:11/23:10/23:54 · Reuters via Al-Monitor · CNN (two US officials, 10:28 ET) · NASA FIRMS/VIIRS (our GIBS check Sep 10)

CONFIRMED — rung 7 PENDING SAM. The smoke plume of Thursday has a statement: 'The East-West pipeline in the Riyadh and Medina regions was subjected to several attacks on Thursday morning … stopped as a precaution, and the attacks resulted in some injuries' (Saudi Energy Ministry, SPA, 19:11 UTC Friday); 'attacked by drones launched from Iraq' (Foreign Ministry, 20:10 UTC) — no militia named, no word 'Iran'; Riyadh will 'give the brotherly Iraqi government an opportunity to take the necessary measures' at PM Al-Zaidi's request while reserving 'all measures necessary to protect its sovereignty'; Baghdad orders an investigation and says its territory will not be 'a launchpad for attacks against any country'. CNN's two US officials: pump stations struck, 'extensive fire damage' at one, drones 'originating from Iraq'; State, White House and CENTCOM declined comment. Our Sep 10 VIIRS check (anomalies at ~24.0N 40.2E/40.7E beside a persistent 40.5E source) now reads as corroboration. What the rules say: Gulf energy hit by an Iranian proxy → rung 7 (actor ir), the 'Iran strikes GCC territory' signal, the 'Gulf energy struck' nudge (force +5, deal −4, grind −1) — all held for Sam's tick; the Saudi pot's 'struck' component moved on its own (84°). What it is not: a Houthi act (no claim from Sanaa, which has been claiming everything), and not — yet — an attributed Iranian order. Tells: a militia claim (Kataib Hezbollah, Nujaba), Tehran's first word, whether Petroline restarts before Monday, Yanbu loadings, whether Riyadh still sits at the Oman table.
Iran: widen the war · Saudi–UAE: forced to escalate — rung 7 + signal HELD
Baghaei via Mehr 247656 (18:00 Tehran) · AFP via ToI · Arab News · Al Jazeera (Tehran correspondent, 18:00 GMT) · Oman Observer / Bloomberg (FT) · Mehr (Araghchi–Faisal)

Tehran sets the table — and writes the caveat in. Baghaei's evening statement: the foreign ministers of 'the Persian Gulf littoral states and the Sea of Oman' — Iran, Iraq and the Gulf states — meet in Oman on Monday; the agenda is 'the outcomes of negotiations between Iran and Oman regarding the establishment of safe routes for commercial shipping'; an understanding on temporary routes exists; Iran is 'committed to ensure the security of navigation' — 'however, as long as aggressive actions and illegal interventions by the United States, including maritime blockades and economic warfare, persist, the security of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz cannot be guaranteed.' Al Jazeera's Tehran correspondent: six GCC states, Iraq and Iran at foreign-minister level, the first such table since the war began; 'not a return to the negotiation table or peace talks … a regional solution to a regional problem', which 'with the assistance and support of the GCC countries may trigger another launch of talks with the United States'. Still no Omani communiqué, no named Gulf confirmation, no lane map. Scored once under the strait-regime rule (07:00); this is the same event. What it is: the MOU track Iran wants, offered to the neighbours with Baghdad in the room, explicitly walled off from 'extra-regional actors'. What it is not: a US–Iran channel — and Washington's only line today was 'we control the strait'. Tells before Monday: Riyadh/Abu Dhabi/Doha confirmations, an Omani statement, the map, whether the IRGC's 'blocked' language softens, whether Washington blesses, ignores or dismisses it.
Iran: deal via Oman · strait regime — Gulf: mediation live — US: watch the answer
UKMTO via Gulf News (03:13 GST) · Mehr 247632/247633 (video) · globalsecurity Day-196 · CENTCOM (silent four days) · Kpler

Two unconfirmed kinetic items at the strait's mouth, both ageing. Khasab: UKMTO 133-26 (19:10 UTC Sep 10) — four unknown projectiles, two unknown vessels, fire aboard one; 47 hours on (18:00 UTC Sep 11) Gulf News still has them 'unidentified', UKMTO attributes to nobody, no casualties reported, no IRGC claim, no Omani statement, no CENTCOM word; rung 5 stands (actor Iran by pattern). The IRGC Navy says it destroyed a US unmanned surface vessel — Saildrone Explorer hull 5838, operated from Khasab since the Bahrain damage, on 'an aggressive mission' — and has released video (Mehr; CBS carried the claim Sep 10); single source, no US confirmation; rung 8 at most if CENTCOM confirms, not set. Kpler counted 7 transits Thursday, none crude; AIS 12 in / 16 out in the 24 h to 17:41 UTC. The longer both stay dark, the more Khasab looks like small craft and the USV like a claim for the home audience — but a named tanker at Khasab would fire the 'tanker seized or fired on' nudge.
Iran: force escalation early · tanker for tanker
AFP via Times of Israel · Euronews · Al Jazeera liveblog (Saree, al-Assad, Hopton) · Reuters · Axios · Al-Masirah

The second chokepoint, finished and framed — and now complete: by Friday afternoon the Houthis held Mayyun (Perim) and the Greater and Lesser Hanish islands, 'everything that was under our control on the western coast has fallen' (Yemeni government official to AFP; Euronews; Al Jazeera). The government's air force says it is striking the Taiz–Mocha road; the UN says the Houthis seized a humanitarian facility in Mocha. Saree's statement: an operation launched Sep 3 expelled 'Saudi-backed forces' from six districts, 5,400 km²; 'maritime navigation remains safe for all companies except Saudi ships'; 'siege with siege and escalation with escalation until the aggression ceases'. Politburo member al-Assad: 'no cause for alarm', navigation 'safe and orderly'. Chatham House's Al-Muslimi: Iran 'gets a lot by having indirect control over Bab al-Mandeb' alongside Hormuz; the Houthis 'will consider this enough for now'. KCL's Krieg: the anti-Houthi front is 'highly fragmented', bought loyalties, UAE and Saudi networks competing. Trump's Thursday refusal of MBS's request for US strikes stands. Not a Hormuz rung; the 'Houthis close the Red Sea' card is live — no rule scored until a ship is attacked; a Saudi-flagged ship is the trigger to watch.

The Council still has no date on the IAEA Board's Sep 9 finding (23–3–8). Thursday's product was the 1737 sanctions-committee fight after an 11–2–2 procedural vote (Russia, China against; Pakistan, Somalia abstaining): the US says the committee 'exists … is operational' and 'will look to partners in the coming days to weigh options'; Britain's MacIntosh says the Charter obliges every member to implement the sanctions resolutions, arms embargo included; France: enough material for 'potentially 10 explosive nuclear devices'. Moscow's Nebenzya: Russia 'won't allow sanctions on Tehran to be reimposed under any circumstances' — 'irresponsible actions' that undermine diplomacy; Beijing votes with him. Tehran's answer is a letter (Darzi: 'abuse of process', 2231 'expired 18 October 2025') and, the same day, a regional Hormuz table. Washington's Friday line was the 9/11 stage: Hegseth 'we will finish this fight', Trump 'Iran will never ever have a nuclear weapon' — rhetoric, no resolution, no date, no strike, and Thursday's refusal of a second front against the Houthis still stands. No movement in the six hours to 22:00 UTC. Reading: the week's evidence favours no-military-option — the Council product is bureaucratic, the White House refuses a second front, the munitions floor is on the record, and the regional track is forming around Washington rather than with it.
